facts.value: Refers to the examination by employers of job applicants' public social media profiles as part of the hiring assessment.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: The vast majority of Fortune 500 companies use social media as a tool to screen prospective employees and for talent acquisition.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: This practice raises ethical questions regarding the access employers have to information that applicants choose to make public.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: Many Western-European countries restrict employers' use of social media in the workplace.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: States such as Arkansas, California, Colorado, Illinois, Maryland, Michigan, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, Utah, Washington, and Wisconsin protect applicants and employees from surrendering usernames and passwords for social media accounts.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: Use of social media has caused significant problems for some applicants who are active on social media.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: A 2013 survey of 17,000 young people in six countries found that one in ten people aged 16 to 34 claimed to have been rejected for a job because of social media activity.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA

facts.value: Social media services have been reported to affect deception in resumes, increasing deception about interests and hobbies.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies) - BA
